answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed wharf berth where the holder works one real cargo-inspection shift a week, stamping cleared manifests with a velvet seal issued in person by the harbor master, one seal per shift and no seal without the shift. A shared reef of bonds backs the wharf: every identity posts a bond in outside money into the reef, and the bond doubles for each further berth on the same funding trail. One operator cannot work two shifts at once, so each extra fake identity costs another berth, another weekly shift, another human, and twice the prior bond.
